label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
Thanks Deirdre, and thank you for asking rather than just announcing it. I understand the numbers, and I can see that Bronwyn needs the help with 24 little ones. I’m not asking for the allocation to be reversed, but I also don’t want to pretend this is an easy change for me. Noma has been with the Seahorses for three years, since my very first year teaching. She basically trained me—sign-in sheets, the parent WhatsApp group, and how to get through the day without losing my mind. I cried in the car this morning, so this one really has landed hard.

The children have that relationship with her too. They ask for “Noma’s song” every day, and when Zayd was having his meltdowns in Term 2, she was the only one who could calm him, sitting with him under the jungle gym. My concern is those first weeks of Grade R: new children crying at the gate, while also adjusting to a brand-new assistant, is a lot at once. It does help that Noma will only be across the courtyard and still on the property, and that Luthando and Mia already know her from aftercare.

Could we please put two practical handover requests to SMT?

1. Could Charlene come in for a day or two in the last week of term, between 1 and 4 December, ahead of her official start on 11 January? It would give her time to meet Noma, see our routines and ask questions before January.
2. Could Noma pop across for morning ring during the first week back from 14 January, even for just 15 minutes? Keeping the isiXhosa songs familiar for those first few mornings would help enormously with settling the children.

I know Grade 00 will need her too, and I don’t want to make Bronwyn’s start harder. I’m just asking that we make the handover proper and gentle—for Charlene and the children as much as for me.
